chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said:
Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'Good character is the best companion.'

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ: Good character or excellent moral conduct

ai.seo_question: What did Ali ibn Abi Talib say is the best companion?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ali (a.s.) metaphorically elevates good character to the status of a 'companion,' highlighting its enduring influence on one's spiritual and social life. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (ethics) as a tangible manifestation of faith, suggesting that moral integrity is more reliable and beneficial than any physical associate. It reflects the broader Imami tradition where inner virtue is seen as the primary determinant of a believer's standing and guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said, “Being good-tempered is the best companion.”
